# `randomTest()` {#fn-randomtest}

The 500-simulation Ggantija-phase workflow in W02 reproduced the bundled global probability, local intervals and adjusted probabilities. [W02 results](w02-field-to-sky.qmd).

In S01, at a nominal 5 percent level the global rejection rate was 4.25 to 5.85 percent across the tested uniform-null settings with sufficient Monte Carlo resolution. Build 2.0.9007 uses the source azimuth density spacing and cutoff for simulations and matches the observed SPD spacing on the shared-horizon route. Refit earlier analyses that used different settings. [S01 results](s01-uniform-orientation.qmd).

**Verified on 2.0.9006.** The global score counts north once. A qualifying excess across north is reported as one interval with start greater than end. [S03 rerun](s03-scoring-checks.qmd).

**Validation on 2.0.9005.** Independent scoring reproduced the stored linear-grid probabilities. A north-crossing azimuth excess can split into two clusters; including both 0 and 360 degrees can also affect the global rank. [S03 results](s03-scoring-checks.qmd).

The null draw relocates each observation’s full measurement model, including triangular asymmetry, taper and independent survey error. [Measurement families](orientation-densities.qmd#measurement-families).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-randomtest)

```{=html}
<p>Following Silva (2020), the test combines the observed measurement densities into a summed probability density (SPD).
For each simulated dataset, the function draws one azimuth per measurement with replacement
from the uniform grid from 0 to 360 degrees at the source azimuth spacing. It applies the
source density family and measurement uncertainties and constructs a comparable SPD.
For a declination test, random azimuths are transformed using the site geometry; the
resulting null distribution in declination depends on latitude and horizon.
</p>
<p>A new transformation takes its atmosphere from <code>skyscapeR.vars</code>. A saved declination PDF supplies its original settings. The fit records these in metadata$atmosphere for declination tests.
</p>
```

**Study design and numerical checks.**

```{=html}
<p>The simulated null describes independently sampled orientations with the
specified site geometry and measurement model. It does not automatically model
shared construction episodes, correlated measurement errors, geographical
clustering or selection of sites after inspecting their orientations. Such
structure needs a justified sampling model or separate sensitivity analysis.
</p>
<p>The pointwise envelope is not a simultaneous confidence band. A significant
global result rejects the specified random-orientation model; it does not
identify a celestial target. Refine the comparison grid and increase
<code>nsims</code> to assess borderline results, preserving the seed and inputs.
More simulations improve Monte Carlo resolution, not the validity of the
archaeological sampling design. Repeated searches over alternative subsets or
models are not included in the within-fit local-cluster adjustment.
</p>



```

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>pdf</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A <em>skyscapeR.pdf</em> object created with either <code>az.pdf</code> or <code>coordtrans</code></p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>az</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Original azimuth <em>skyscapeR.pdf</em>; required only when <code>pdf</code>
contains declination distributions. Must match its distribution count and
order. Do not supply this argument when <code>pdf</code> already contains azimuths.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>hor</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>For azimuth input, optionally supply one shared <em>skyscapeR.horizon</em>
to test in declination. For declination input, required: the original shared
horizon or an ordered list matching the distributions in <code>pdf</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>nsims</code></th><td><code>1000</code></td><td><p>Number of simulations, at least two. Default is 1000.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>conf</code></th><td><code>0.95</code></td><td><p>Confidence level as a fraction. For example, 0.95 requests a 95 percent envelope.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>tails</code></th><td><code>2</code></td><td><p>1 for upper excesses, 2 for excesses and deficits (default).</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>normalise</code></th><td><code>F</code></td><td><p>Logical to control whether to normalize SPDs. Default is FALSE</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.res</code></th><td><code>0.1</code></td><td><p>Resolution with which to output probability distribution(s). Default is 0.1 degrees.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>ncores</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Worker count. By default use half the detected available logical cores, rounded down with a minimum of one. Set ncores=1 for serial execution. The simulation count and memory batch size can further limit workers. Verbose output reports the effective count.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>T</code></td><td><p>Logical. Display progress or informational messages. Default <code>TRUE</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A <em>skyscapeR.sigTest</em> list containing metadata (test settings,
global and local p-values) and data (empirical SPD and null confidence envelope).
No original PDFs or horizon objects are attached.
</p>
```
